location.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
location.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
location.notes: Three distinct regions described for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers are reported in the main text; only aggregate counts and summary statistics per cohort/subgroup.

sample_id.notes: No individual sample identifiers provided in the text; sample counts are given as aggregates (e.g., 44, 50, 68 metagenomes).

subcohort.evidence_quote: 23 adults, avg age (yrs): 33.14 (s.d.: 6.61), range: 20-45... 25 children, avg age (yrs): 6.81
subcohort.notes: Subgroups derived from the reported age-category breakdowns (adults/children/infants) within each country cohort.

control.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
control.notes: Subjects described as healthy but not explicitly assigned a case/control role within a disease study design; the case-control framework applies to separate publicly available disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, etc.), not to the Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts.

body_site.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from a Ghanaian cohort
body_site.notes: All subjects sampled via fecal/stool metagenomics.

days_from_first_collection.notes: No longitudinal sampling or repeat-visit timing was reported for these cohorts.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: the local occupation is subsistence farming and the wider economy based on farming cash crops such as cocoa and plantain
lifestyle.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
lifestyle.notes: Ghana and Tanzania cohorts described with farming/agriculture-based economies; Ethiopia cohort lifestyle is not explicitly characterized in text beyond being non-Westernized.

westernized.evidence_quote: We also sequenced two non-Westernized populations from Ghana and Tanzania.
westernized.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
westernized.notes: Ethiopia also explicitly described as a non-Westernized cohort (paired infant and mother samples from Ethiopia).

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Raw sequencing data (Ghana) This study NCBI-SRA BioProject: PRJNA529124
ncbi_accession.notes: BioProject-level accessions reported per country cohort; no per-sample SRA run accessions given in main text.

age.notes: Mean ages reported per subgroup; granularity is subgroup_level (not per-sample).

age_group.notes: Derived from reported age ranges mapped to schema age-group definitions (e.g., Child: >=2 & <11; Infant: >=1mo & <2yrs); Ghana/Tanzania 'children' ranges include ages <2 so some overlap with Infant category exists but paper uses single label 'children'.

family.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
family.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family.notes: Family-based sampling is described (12 families in Ghana, 18 in Tanzania, mother-infant pairs in Ethiopia) but individual family identifiers are not given in the main text.

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.
family_role.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family_role.notes: Ghana and Tanzania described as 'extended families' without explicit mother/father/child role breakdown.

sex.evidence_quote: 24 adults, avg age (yrs): 29.35 (s.d. 6.24), range: 22-45, sex: 100% female
sex.notes: Other subgroups report mixed-sex percentages (e.g., Ghana adults 52.2% female/47.8% male) rather than a single categorical value, so left as not_reported; see notes for percentages: Ghana adults 52.2% F/47.8% M; Tanzania adults 48.65% F/51.35% M.

bmi.evidence_quote: we considered if the P.copri complex could be associated with other factors such as body mass index (BMI) or age (Table S1)
bmi.section: Results — Associating P. copri Clades with Metagenomically Investigated Human Diseases
bmi.notes: BMI was analyzed as a covariate across disease cohorts in Table S1 but numeric BMI values for the Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts are not given in the main text.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.

disease_details.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease_details.notes: This refers to the newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia). The paper also analyzed publicly available disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) in a secondary meta-analysis of P. copri clade associations with disease, but these were not primary subjects recruited by this study and no per-subject disease status was reported for them here.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Paper concerns gut microbiome genomics, no tumor/residual-disease measurements reported.

study_name.notes: Derived from first author surname (Tett) and publication year (2019) following common study-naming convention; not explicitly stated as a study identifier in the text.

pmid.notes: PMID provided as paper_id in the input metadata, not found verbatim within the body text.

target_condition.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
target_condition.notes: The study's newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia) were healthy; disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) were only used as secondary public meta-analysis datasets, not the primary study population.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted using the PowerSoil DNA isolation kit (Qiagen) as previously described
dna_extraction_kit.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Also used for isolate DNA: 'collected for genomic DNA isolation with the PowerSoil DNA isolation kit (Qiagen).'

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq2500 100nt paired end platform with a target depth of 5Gb/sample
sequencing_platform.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
sequencing_platform.notes: Also isolate sequencing used HiSeq2500: 'Libraries were prepared for sequencing on the HiSeq2500 platform with the TruSeq DNA PCR-free Library Prep Kit (Illumina).' Ancient samples used HiSeqX and HiSeq2500 platforms for different sample types.

host_species.evidence_quote: All subjects enrolled in this study included infants and adults from Ghana, Tanzania and Ethiopia

extraction_warnings: No per-sample tables (Table S1, S2, S4, S5) were included in the provided text; only aggregate/subgroup-level statistics from the Experimental Model and Subject Details section could be extracted.

Schema fields oriented toward sample-level metadata (subject_id, sample_id, probing_pocket_depth, zigosity, etc.) are largely not_reported because the paper only provides cohort-level summary statistics for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania).

Sex distributions for Ghana and Tanzania subgroups are reported as percentages (mixed male/female) rather than a single categorical value, so the enum 'sex' field could not be populated for those subgroups without fabricating per-sample values.

The 'control' enum field (Study Control/Case/Not Used) does not map cleanly onto the healthy, non-disease-focused Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts, which are distinct from the disease case-control cohorts (CRC, T2D, IBD, etc.) analyzed elsewhere in the paper; left as not_reported.
Lifestyle classification (e.g., Agriculturalist) was inferred from economic/occupational descriptions rather than an explicit lifestyle label, lowering confidence.

Batch 1 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Ghana_adults', 'Ghana_children', 'Ethiopia_adults', 'Ethiopia_infants', 'Tanzania_adults', 'Tanzania_children']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a microbiome genomics study (P. copri population genomics), not a clinical/treatment study; most schema fields (disease response, treatment, tumor staging, biomarkers, neonatal/obgyn fields) are not applicable and were not reported.

Disease conditions (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) were analyzed only via meta-analysis of previously published external datasets for clade-disease association testing, not as primary subject-level disease annotations in this study, so disease_details was limited to the 'Healthy' status explicitly reported for the newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania).
No participant-level clinical, treatment, or outcome data were found for disease_response, biomarker, tumor staging, or neonatal/obgyn fields in the main text or STAR Methods.
